title: test(types): make the object-calendar annotation pin able to fail for the class it names
body:
Fixes #9676

Clause-②: no — repairing a blind pin neither widens an accepted set nor enlarges a published surface. Measured and unchanged: the guard answers NOT GOVERNED for both changed paths, and `check:changeset-presence` scores the diff as one released package's source with an empty-frontmatter declaration.

## The choice, and why

The card named two blindnesses in the row asserting 「No bare `object-calendar` literal is left unannotated on the page」. I re-measured both on this branch's head rather than inheriting the filing seat's readings, and found a **third** that decides the route. Four samples through the retired pattern:

| sample | retired pattern |
|---|---|
| column 0, discriminant first | **matches** |
| the same text indented by two | `null` |
| column 0, discriminant **second** | `null` |
| indented, **no discriminant at all** | `null` |

Rows two and three are the card's two blindnesses, confirmed. Row four is the one that settles the choice the dispatch offered: the anchor and the member-order requirement are both loosenable, but a literal that omits the discriminant entirely — the failure mode the page's own prose is about, and the shape of the specimen the card found — is invisible to **any** pattern keyed on `type: 'object-calendar'`, at every anchor and in every member order. Widening the regex would have shut two of the three while still reading as a repair.

So this takes the second route the dispatch named: **replace the pattern with a reading that enumerates the literals.** Every `const NAME = { … }` declaration inside a fence is brace-matched out, then classified as an `object-calendar` literal by either of two independent signals — the discriminant among the literal's **own** members (any indentation, any position), or the literal being handed to an `ObjectCalendar` JSX element (spelled out in words here, since an angle-bracket-shaped token does not survive GitHub's body sanitizer) as its `schema` prop. Neither signal alone can hide a member of the class.

Scope is the **fence**, not the page: `schema` is declared five times on this page in five separate blocks, so a page-wide name match reads the `calendar-view` fragment's `const schema` as the one `ObjectCalendar` consumes and goes red on a healthy page. That was measured, not guessed — the first prototype did exactly that.

### Where the repaired row still cannot fail

Stated here and in the docblock rather than left for the comment to over-claim a second time: a literal carrying **neither** the discriminant **nor** an `ObjectCalendar` consumption inside its own fence remains invisible. Nothing in the page text identifies such a literal as an `object-calendar` at all, so that is the boundary of the claim, not a gap in the reading — and the row is named to that boundary.

## Premise check — one half of the card is now stale, and it matters

The card's structural claim holds: the pattern is still in the tree and still blind in the two ways it names, plus the third above.

Its **live specimen** is gone. PR objectui#9678 (`bb2d33570`, 「Part of #7311」, merged about an hour after this card was filed) annotated the Direct Component Usage block and gave it the discriminant. The literal the card quotes verbatim is no longer on the page, so a repair landing today is green on arrival — which is precisely the condition under which a pin repair can be mistaken for a measurement. That is why the proof below runs against the page as it stood **before** that merge.

## Reverse verification — two legs, on the real historical specimen

Both legs run against `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` restored to `bb2d33570^` by a path-scoped checkout from a pinned commit, with the mutation proven on disk before anything was read. Occurrences of the specimen's opening line went 0 to 1 and of the annotated spelling 1 to 0; the page's blob hash moved off its `HEAD` value.

- **Leg A — the repaired pin against that page: RED.** `Tests 1 failed | 20 passed (21)`, `AssertionError: content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx: these `object-calendar` literals carry no type annotation: expected [ 'schema' ] to deeply equal []`. It names the literal.
- **Leg B — the pre-repair pin against the *same* page: GREEN.** `Tests 19 passed (19)`, exit 0. That is the false green the card is about, reproduced.

Restore verified by blob hash equality against `HEAD` for both mutated paths, plus empty `git diff HEAD`, empty `git diff --cached` and empty `git status --short`. The whole run sat under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restoring from `HEAD` by absolute path. No permanent artefact of either leg is in the diff.

## Ability to fail is pinned, not asserted

One new row feeds both previously blind shapes through the reading as self-contained one-fence pages and asserts each is reported unannotated, keeping the retired pattern beside them as a **negative control** that must miss both. The annotated variants of the same two must come back clean, so the row is refusing the missing annotation and not the indentation. A second control inside the main row requires the fence split to lose no declaration, and a third requires the reader to see a named population — `every()` over an empty set is the same silent green this card was filed for.

## Tests

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/object-calendar-record-source-7313.test.ts` — `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 21 passed (21)`, exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` — `Test Files 207 passed (207)`, `Tests 4816 passed (4816)`, exit 0 (under the shared verify lock; `VERDICT command-exit 0`).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` — exit 0. Its script runs `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.examples.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the test source is inside the checked set rather than assumed to be.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types lint` — exit 0, `0 errors, 290 warnings`, every warning pre-existing; the one in this file is on a line this branch does not touch.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` — OK. `pnpm check:new-line-citations` — `0 new citation(s)`, exit 0. `pnpm check:changeset-claims` — exit 0, no finding naming this changeset. `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` — OK. `pnpm check:test-path-roots` — OK.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — exit 0 with the empty-frontmatter declaration; `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — exit 0.
- Narrowing declared: repo-wide `turbo run lint`, `turbo run type-check` and the full `vitest run` are left to CI. What ran here is the affected package's own lint, type-check and suite, plus every gate whose input this diff touches.

The changeset declares an empty frontmatter. Measured after a build of this package: the symbols this change adds appear in zero files under `dist`, this package's only published code path, while the control symbol `ObjectCalendarSchema` appears in six; no file under `__tests__` reaches `dist`.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, noted and **not** filed — neither reaches the three filing classes, and the handoff for each is named:

- The retired pattern's shape (a `^`-anchored, `m`-flagged, first-member-ordered literal match asserted `.toBeNull()`) may appear in sibling pins under the same directory. The card explicitly declines to measure that, and so does this branch — a sweep is a separate, wider question. Handoff: no specific PR or person; it needs a dispatch of its own to be anything but a guess.
- `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` carries one unannotated `const schema = { type: 'calendar-view', … }` in the 「Allowing event creation」 fragment. It is correctly excluded by this row (it is not an `object-calendar` literal), and it is a deliberate fragment whose accompanying doc-snippet note records its measured compile errors — annotating it would move that measurement. Handoff: whoever next edits that fragment; not addressed here.

Neither is a reproducible defect, a declared-contract breach, or a trap producing metadata a runtime refuses, so neither is filed.
